notes.text: Eventually always b — FG b, the language with no deterministic Büchi automaton. Here it is, deterministic. The machine is shaped exactly like the DBA for "infinitely often a"; the acceptance condition is what differs. Under co-Büchi the ringed states are the ones that must STOP happening: a run is accepting when inf(r) ∩ F = ∅.

"last was a" is entered on exactly the a's, so visiting it finitely often means the word has finitely many a's. Compare the Büchi model's "eventually always b", which needs a nondeterministic guess to say the same thing. co-Büchi does not need the guess — nondeterminism buys it nothing at all, because NcoBA = DcoBA.

meta.title: Eventually always b
meta.blurb: FG b as a deterministic co-Büchi automaton — the same language a Büchi automaton can only recognise by guessing. Swapping α from Büchi to co-Büchi is the entire difference.
